clue.text: Journey westward among trees in French city

indicators.note: being among things means sitting inside them, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: lime trees, also called lindens

indicators.note: in an across entry, going west means reading right to left, so the word is turned round

parts.note: a go is a trip or turn, a journey

explanation.surface: A traveller heads west through the woods somewhere in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Limoges is a city in west-central France, famous for its porcelain.

clue.text: Puzzle initially freaking out clumsy idiot

indicators.note: out means removed, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: to flummox is to baffle or puzzle

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word after it

parts.note: the first letter of freaking

explanation.surface: A crossword baffles someone who starts panicking, a hopeless dolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A lummox is a big awkward, slow-witted person, an informal word for a clumsy oaf.

clue.text: Fashion house given mention

indicators.note: given mention means spoken of, so the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: a manor is a large country house

explanation.surface: A couture house gets a mention in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion house' reads as one phrase, but Fashion is the definition and house the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashion as a noun can mean a way of doing something, as in 'after a fashion', which is a manner.

clue.text: Ah! Geometry transformational in maths branch!

indicators.note: transformational means changing form, so the letters take a new shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A student exclaims at discovering transformational geometry, a real topic in maths.
explanation.definitionFit: Game theory is a branch of mathematics studying strategic decisions between competing players.

clue.text: King opening up sees PM

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters are turned round

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
a bodily opening

explanation.surface: The King opens his weekly audience with the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi Sunak was UK Prime Minister from 2022 to 2024; the earthy 'opening' is the setter's joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Rishi Sunak was the British prime minister when this puzzle appeared, so PM defines him by example.

clue.text: Greens, at first boiled, mashed: many thanks!

indicators.note: mashed food is pulped out of shape, so the letters lose their order
at first asks for only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of Greens
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner thanks the cook for vegetables boiled then mashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'Much obliged!' is an old-fashioned way of expressing gratitude, so the word works as an exclamation of thanks.

clue.text: Ring that goes with fancy earrings in storage container

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the word after it is made over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ring is kept with some showy earrings in a jewellery box.
explanation.definitionFit: An organiser is a box or case with compartments for keeping things tidy, so a storage container.

clue.text: Holding back eighth item to be auctioned?

parts.note: each item in an auction is a lot
H is the eighth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A bidder waits for the eighth item in the sale, lot H.
explanation.walkthrough: Auction lots are sometimes lettered, so the eighth would be Lot H; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Loth (also spelt loath) means reluctant, unwilling, which is holding back.

clue.text: In crowd Scots frightened posh student

indicators.note: In places what follows inside the word for a crowd

parts.note: the gate is the attendance at a sports match
rad is a Scots word for afraid
U means upper-class

explanation.surface: A posh student is scared to be among a crowd of Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: A graduate is someone who has completed a degree, and in the US a graduate student continues study.

clue.text: Actor once in Parliament full of comic potential

parts.note: a diet is a legislative assembly, as in the Japanese Diet or the Diet of Worms
rich, as in 'that's rich', means ripe for laughs

explanation.surface: An actor who became an MP proved a gift for comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich was a German-American film star of the 1930s and later, so an actor of former times.

clue.text: Beat somewhat shorter finalist in Omnium?

parts.note: mini means smaller or shorter than usual, as in a miniskirt

indicators.note: the finalist of a word is the one that comes last, its closing letter

parts.note: the last letter of Omnium

explanation.surface: A track cyclist who made the Omnium final turns out to be a little shorter than the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Omnium is a multi-race track cycling event, which makes 'Beat' look like a verb about winning; it is a musical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a half note, which counts as one beat in time signatures such as 2/2.

clue.text: Horrid thing to ruin repose, ultimately?

definitions.text: Horrid thing to ruin repose, ultimately

indicators.note: something horrid is ugly and distorted, so the word after it is scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
to mar is to spoil or ruin

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of repose

explanation.surface: Asks what horrible thing finally wrecks a good night's rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a bad dream is the horrid thing that ruins sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is a frightening dream, the kind of horror that destroys peaceful sleep.

clue.text: Public article to appear before Charles's passing

parts.note: overt means done openly, in public
the indefinite article
Charles III is the British king

explanation.surface: A public notice heralds the death of King Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' looks like death in the surface; here it is a driver going past another vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtaking is moving past a slower vehicle on the road, which is also called passing.

clue.text: Rhine tributary rougher here and there

indicators.note: here and there means only at intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of rougher

explanation.surface: A river feeding the Rhine runs choppier in places.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ruhr is a German river that flows into the Rhine at Duisburg, giving its name to the industrial region.

clue.text: Boring President forced to tour America

indicators.note: touring a place means going all round it, so these letters surround another
forced means pushed out of its natural shape, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
A is a standard abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A dull head of state is made to go on a tour of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian as an adjective means dull and uninspired, lacking any flair.

clue.text: One in secret coup destroyed ERG politician?

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the other letters
something destroyed is broken apart, so the two words are reassembled in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A plotter is caught in a failed covert power grab within a party faction.
explanation.walkthrough: The ERG is the European Research Group, a caucus of Brexit-supporting Conservative MPs; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the ERG are known for opposing the European Union, the defining stance of a Eurosceptic.

clue.text: Agent with servant brought in free carpet

parts.note: a rep, or representative, acts as an agent

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside, so one piece is held by another

parts.note: to rid is to free of something
a manservant

explanation.surface: A salesman and his servant come round to lay a carpet at no charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' looks like a floor covering but is a verb: to carpet someone is British slang for to scold them.
explanation.definitionFit: To be carpeted is to be called before the boss for a telling-off, so carpet means to rebuke.

clue.text: Drive away from island and lake in Kansas City

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the city's name

parts.note: Dodge City is a city in Kansas, famed in Wild West lore
Is. is the abbreviation for island
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A road trip leaves an island and a lake for Kansas City, Missouri.
explanation.walkthrough: Kansas City is a real city, but here it means a city in Kansas: Dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge something is to force it out of position, to drive it away.

clue.text: Pedant needs to stay alert in the middle

parts.note: to stick is to stay put

indicators.note: in the middle keeps only the central letters of the word

parts.note: the middle three letters of alert

explanation.surface: A nitpicker must stay watchful at the centre of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on strict rules and correctness, which is what a pedant does.

clue.text: Printer's perseverance keeping dot?

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the answer sits inside the run of words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A dogged printer insists on a dot, perhaps a full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: To dot something about is to scatter it at intervals, the same as interspersing it.

clue.text: Tinker's award for service announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken aloud, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: a medal is awarded for service

explanation.surface: A travelling tinker's military honour is made public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinker's' reads as possessive; it is 'Tinker is', with tinker a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To tinker with something is to fiddle with it unhelpfully, which is to meddle.

clue.text: Map book linked to temperature in the end

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A map book is eventually tied to temperature readings, as in a climate atlas.
explanation.definitionFit: At last and in the end both mean finally, after a long wait.

clue.text: Want chess player to sacrifice bishop

indicators.note: to sacrifice is to give up, so a letter is lost from the word

parts.note: the two sides in chess are White and Black
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A chess player is urged to give up a bishop for an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Want as a noun means a shortage or absence, the same as lack.

clue.text: Stormy setter sloshed in shopping sector

parts.note: high means intoxicated, like sloshed

indicators.note: a stormy thing is wild and turbulent, so the word after it is thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crossword setter, drunk and in a temper, is out on the town among the shops.
explanation.definitionFit: The high street is a town's main road, where most of its shops are found.

clue.text: Sailor almost showing courage

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: 'my hearties' is how pirates address fellow sailors

explanation.surface: A sailor almost displays bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart means courage or spirit, as in 'take heart' or 'lose heart'.

clue.text: Russian fighter protecting name for dynasty

indicators.note: protecting means guarding by surrounding, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter jet
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A Russian jet guards the name of a royal line.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644.

clue.text: Buddhist artist engaging a wool producer reportedly

indicators.note: engaging here means taking on or holding, so the artist's name wraps the letter

parts.note: Salvador Dali, the Surrealist painter
taken as written

indicators.note: reportedly means as said out loud, so the sound counts and not the spelling

parts.note: the llama is an Andean animal kept for its wool

explanation.surface: A Buddhist painter takes on a sheep or similar animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalai Lama is the spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism, so a Buddhist by example.

clue.text: I may represent this country

parts.note: surface reading: someone claims they could stand for their nation, as a diplomat or athlete
setter's reading: the letter I, whose code word in the NATO phonetic alphabet is a country's name

explanation.walkthrough: In radio spelling, Alpha, Bravo, Charlie and so on, the letter I is spoken as the name of a large South Asian country.
explanation.definitionFit: India is both a nation and the phonetic alphabet word that stands for the letter I.

clue.text: Exasperated striker's last time in terminus

indicators.note: in places those letters inside the word that follows

parts.note: a terminus is the end of the line

indicators.note: last asks for just the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of striker
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A footballer is furious after a last-minute goal at the end of the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Exasperated and enraged both mean made very angry.

clue.text: An outside line to ring?

parts.note: surface reading: an external telephone line used to call someone
setter's reading: in geometry, a straight line lying outside a circle that just touches it

explanation.walkthrough: The ring is a circle, not a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangent is a straight line touching a curve at exactly one point without crossing it.
